channel.title: Cork Safety Alerts - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Cork Safety Alerts (corksafetyalerts.com)

item.title: Yellow Weather Warnings Issued as Frost, Ice and Heavy Rain Set to Impact Ireland
item.description: Yellow weather warnings issued as frost, ice and heavy rain are set to impact Ireland and parts of Munster this weekend. Stay safe and plan ahead.

item.title: Collision on N25 Killeagh/Youghal
item.description: Reports of a collision on the N25 between Killeagh and Youghal just beyond Burgess. Emergency services are en route. Take care on approach.

item.title: Collision on R522 Doneraile
item.description: Reports of a collision on R522 Doneraile near the junction with Park North. Emergency services are en route. Take care on approach.

item.title: Multi-vehicle Collision on N40 Westbound
item.description: Reports of a multi-vehicle collision, westbound, on the N40 South Ring Road between Junction 9 (N28) Ringaskiddy and Junction 8 Douglas (Cork). Take care on approach.Source: TII Traffic Alerts, 13 February at 16:00.

item.title: Freemount Water Mains Upgrade to Improve Reliability and Reduce Future Disruptions
item.description: Water mains upgrade begins in Freemount next week, with works set to improve reliability and reduce future supply disruptions.

item.title: R630 Active Travel Project to Retain Two Lanes as Works Progress, Council Confirms
item.description: Update issued on R630 Whitegate Road works, with two lanes retained and major safety, lighting and public transport upgrades progressing.

item.title: Independent Report Finds State Response to Blackwater Fish Kill Was Swift, with Improvements Identified
item.description: Independent review finds agencies acted quickly during the Blackwater fish kill, with new steps planned to improve detection, coordination and prevention.

item.title: Councillor Honore Kamegni Calls for 30km/h Default Speed Limit Across Cork City
item.description: Cork City Councillor calls for a default 30km/h speed limit in built-up areas across Cork City to improve safety and quality of life.
